messages:
marta (Marketing): ok team — we need a clear, single-sheet narrative for the upcoming benchmark push. focus: throughput economics (how latency interacts with $/token and cost per inference). target: devs for PLG and infra buyers. can we list candidate headlines and 3 chart ideas?
jake (PMM): quick thought — headline should be benefit-first: 'Same accuracy, lower serving costs' vs technical: 'Latency-aware batching yields 3x cost savings'. prefer benefit-first for blog/ads.
sam (Product): agree benefit-first for top-funnel. technical blog + appendix for the infra crowd. chart ideas: 1) cost per 1M tokens vs average latency 2) throughput (tokens/s) vs model size 3) tail-latency distribution under batching.
lucy (Design): can we avoid too many line charts? suggest one hero chart (stacked area showing cumulative cost savings over time), then two small multiples for latency vs cost by workload. i'll mock two sketches.
derek (Growth): inbound routing note: capture lead intent in webinar signups — add radio for 'I care about: latency / cost / compliance / all'. route cost/throughput leads to growth SDRs, infra/compliance to AE. also add hidden field for avg_token_rate.
marta (Marketing): good — messaging A/B test idea: A: 'Cut inference spend by up to 70% without sacrificing latency' B: 'Predictable latency, lower cost: how we make LLMs economical'. which do we run on paid?
jake (PMM): run B on developer audiences and A on finance/ops audiences. devs respond to predictability. finance likes big % numbers.
bench-bot: Automated benchmark output: model=xlarge-v2, q=4bit, avg_latency=52ms, p95=120ms, tokens_per_sec=1900, cost_per_1k_tokens=$0.0028
sam (Product): bench-bot numbers look promising. we should annotate hero claim with the workload: 'conversational 4-turn prompts, 2k tokens/day'. don't make blanket claims.
lucy (Design): noted. i'll add a tooltip/footnote area in the hero viz for workload knobs. also want a tiny explainer for batching and KV cache.
derek (Growth): webinar hook: 'Real numbers: serving 10M real user requests — what we changed and how much you save'. include live Q&A and a two-minute demo of route fallback. CTA: request eval credits.
marta (Marketing): timeline — blog + charts draft by Mon, landing + ad copy Tue, webinar Wed week after. is that realistic?
jake (PMM): tight but doable if Product provides annotated bench table today. i'll draft two headline variants and 3 short descriptions for ads.
sam (Product): i'll export the bench CSV and include config: batch_size, seq_len_dist, hardware_type. sending now.
bench-bot: Attached: /bench/exports/1819000123-xlargev2-export.csv (contains latency, p50, p95, tokens/sec, cost_estimates)
lucy (Design): receipt. will push initial sketches to Figma and link in thread. need copy for callouts, marta plz provide hero sentence.
marta (Marketing): hero sentence draft: 'Run LLMs that feel instantaneous — while cutting serving costs by up to 3x for typical chat workloads.' feedback?\ake (typo): (this message intentionally left as a typo to simulate short slack chatter)
jake (PMM): minor tweak: "Run LLMs that feel instantaneous — and cut serving costs up to 3x for typical chat workloads." remove 'by' and tighten.
sam (Product): +1. also add microdisclaimer: 'Savings depend on model and workload; see benchmark appendix.'
derek (Growth): for ad copy: short lines: 1) 'Predictable latency. Predictable spend.' 2) 'Serve more convo traffic for less.' 3) 'From prototype to production: inference that scales economically.'
lucy (Design): going to try a hero visual: two bars — 'baseline' vs 'Redwood-configured' with latency band and cost band. simple.
marta (Marketing): routing ops: action items — jake write PMM lines, lucy designs by Tue EOD, sam share final CSV now, derek set webinar registration funnel and routing, I'll draft blog by Mon. any blockers?
jake (PMM): none from me.
sam (Product): CSV shared, bench config in thread, no blockers.
derek (Growth): need SDR capacity — I'll confirm headcount, might need to cap leads for first wave.
marta (Marketing): ok — we'll cap. final ask: everyone add one sentence on why this benchmark matters to your audience. i'll compile.
bench-bot: Note: p99 tail sensitive to burst size — recommend calling out p95 and p99 separately in appendix.
marta (Marketing): perfect. thanks all — I'll compile sentences and post final draft here for signoff before publishing. :rocket:
